s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic mucocutaneous blistering disorder with oral and skin involvement
salient_findings: Presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the lower lip, oral cavity, face, trunk, and extremities
Skin biopsy showing spongiosis, neutrophils with nuclear dust, and superficial perivascular dermatitis
key_facts: 39-year-old woman with no significant medical history
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes
Small bullae, erosions, and crusts on the lower lip
Erosions with epithelized mucosa in the oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions over erythematous and cicatricial lesions on the face, trunk, and extremities
Normal chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography
Normal gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis
Superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Negative direct immunofluorescence for IgG, IgA, and C3
Negative indirect immunofluorescence using normal human skin and 1-molar sodium chloride–split normal human skin
Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, which is characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Mucocutaneous lesions with oral and skin involvement, consistent with pemphigus vulgaris

shortlist.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Oral and skin involvement with blistering lesions, which can be seen in mucous membrane pemphigoid

shortlist.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with crusts and erosions, which can be seen in pemphigus foliaceus

shortlist.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Blistering lesions with linear IgA deposits, although not directly mentioned, it's a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation

raw.rationale: The presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, as well as the clinical findings of mucocutaneous lesions and the histopathological features, are consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: Negative direct and indirect immunofluorescence for IgG, IgA, and C3, and lack of antibodies to Dsg1 and Dsg3

rejected.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
rejected.why: Negative direct and indirect immunofluorescence, and lack of antibodies to BP180 and BP230

rejected.label: Pemphigus foliaceus
rejected.why: Clinical and histopathological features do not match, and lack of antibodies to Dsg1

rejected.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
rejected.why: Negative direct and indirect immunofluorescence, and lack of linear IgA deposits at the basement membrane zone
